The course content is available under [CC BY 4.0](/LICENSE-CCBY.md). You can copy it, change it, and teach it, if you give credit. This page explains how the site is built.

## Where the content lives

- `index.qmd` — landing page, with the course facts and the learning outcomes
- `contents/course-description.qmd` — the long course description
- `contents/syllabus.qmd` — the session plan for both days and the assessment rules
- `contents/sessions/` — one page for each of the 12 sessions
- `contents/assignments.qmd` — the work between and after the two days
- `contents/literature.qmd` — the two course texts and the required sections
- `contents/resources.qmd` — course material and optional learning resources
- `contents/cheat-sheet.qmd` — the statistics cheat sheet
- `contents/about.qmd` — format, teaching approach, and contact
- `references.bib` — BibTeX entries for every cited work
- `_quarto.yml` — navigation, theme, and site metadata
- `_brand.yml` and `theme.scss` — the greyscale palette, the IBM Plex fonts, and the callout colours

Each session page follows the same structure: an at-a-glance table, the reading, a reading summary, the in-class work, and the output.

## Build the site locally

You need Node.js 24 or later, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org/).

1. Clone the repository.
2. Run `npm install`.
3. Run `npm run prepare` to install the Git hooks.
4. Run `npm run preview`.

The preview server reloads the site after each change.

## How the cheat sheet works

`contents/cheat-sheet.qmd` builds every figure with static Python. Quarto runs the `{python}` cells at build time and embeds the images. The published site is plain HTML.

The front matter sets `echo: false`, so the page shows figures and not code. The first cell sets the chart colours and the matplotlib defaults. Every later cell reuses them.

The figures need matplotlib, numpy, and pandas. All three are dev dependencies in `pyproject.toml`. Run `uv sync` after a clone.

Flows, trees, and sets of relations use [Mermaid](https://mermaid.js.org/) diagrams instead of figures. Prefer a diagram when the content is a structure rather than a distribution.

::: {.callout-caution title="Look at the rendered page"}
Check that every figure draws and that no axis label is clipped. A figure that is too small for its labels still renders without an error.
:::

## Adapt the course

1. Fork the repository.
2. Edit the pages in `contents/`.
3. Update the title, the URLs, and the navigation in `_quarto.yml`.
4. Update `_brand.yml`, `CITATION.cff`, and `README.md` with your own values.
5. Replace the favicons at the repository root.
6. Enable GitHub Pages in the repository settings with the source **GitHub Actions**.
7. Push to `main`. The workflow `.github/workflows/quarto-publish.yml` deploys the site.
